misconceptions.description: Treating momentum as a magnitude-only quantity
misconceptions.trigger: learner ignores sign or direction in a one-dimensional collision
misconceptions.feedback: Momentum is a vector. In one-dimensional problems, the sign convention carries that direction information. Leftward and rightward velocities cannot be added as if they were all positive.

misconceptions.description: Assuming kinetic energy is conserved in every collision
misconceptions.trigger: learner uses both momentum and kinetic-energy conservation in an inelastic collision
misconceptions.feedback: Momentum is conserved in isolated collisions, but kinetic energy is conserved only in elastic collisions. In a perfectly inelastic collision, the bodies stick and kinetic energy decreases.

misconceptions.description: Using momentum conservation without checking the external impulse assumption
misconceptions.trigger: learner applies conservation of momentum to a system with significant external forces over the interval
misconceptions.feedback: Conservation of momentum is a system statement that requires negligible external impulse. Start by defining the system and checking whether the collision interval is short enough for external effects to be ignored.

misconceptions.trigger: learner omits the time interval or the area-under-curve idea
misconceptions.feedback: Impulse measures the accumulated effect of force over time. Use J = integral(F dt), or J = F_avg delta t when an average force is appropriate.
